why: Both D.R. Horton and Century Communities are US national homebuilders that design, build, and sell new single-family homes and townhomes directly to individual homebuyers (entry-level and move-up), and both operate affiliated mortgage and title services for those same buyers. The evidence shows near-identical products, customer segments, business models, revenue models, value-chain positions, and distribution channels. The only notable difference is scale (D.R. Horton is the larger of the two), but scale alone does not disqualify a comp at this level of business similarity.
reason: Same primary product (new single-family homes/townhomes sold to individual homebuyers), same customer base (entry-level and move-up B2C buyers), same ancillary services (mortgage, title), same distribution (on-site sales staff + third-party brokers), same value-chain position (land acquirer → builder → direct seller), and same US national geography. This satisfies the "same product AND same customers" criterion for a score of 2.

primary_products.reason: Both build and sell new single-family homes and townhomes. Century also adds condos/paired homes, a minor difference that does not reduce overlap materially.

primary_services.reason: Both offer mortgage financing, title insurance/settlement services, and home insurance to their homebuyers through dedicated subsidiaries.

customer_segment.reason: Both sell to individual (B2C) homebuyers, including first-time and move-up buyers.

end_markets.reason: Both operate in the US residential housing / new-home construction market.

business_model.reason: Both are homebuilders that acquire land, build homes using subcontractors, and sell directly to buyers, with affiliated financial services.

revenue_model.reason: Both earn revenue primarily from home sales and secondarily from mortgage origination and title/closing fees.

value_chain_position.reason: Both sit at the OEM/builder level: they acquire land, construct homes, and sell directly to end buyers.

geography_served.reason: Both serve US national markets. D.R. Horton is present in more states (described as America's largest builder across the full country); Century is in 16 states / 45+ markets. Broad overlap but D.R. Horton has wider coverage.

specialization.reason: Both specialize in residential homebuilding with affiliated mortgage and title services—no material difference in specialization profile.

distribution_channels.reason: Both use on-site sales staff at model/community homes, third-party real estate brokers, and online channels for home sales.

regulatory_exposure.reason: Both face land-use/zoning/building code regulation for homebuilding and CFPB/RESPA mortgage lending rules for their financial services subsidiaries.
